content: Aluminum hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide are typically prescribed in doses of 10-20 mL orally between meals and at bedtime for individuals over 12 years of age. The safety and efficacy of these medications have not been established for children under 12 years of age. Aluminum hydroxide can reduce the effectiveness of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH, which affects its absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated, and it is recommended to avoid using drugs that raise gastric pH with pazopanib. If necessary, short-acting antacids may be used instead of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) or H2 antagonists, but the dosing of antacids and pazopanib should be separated by several hours. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of raltegravir by binding to cations in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. This interaction is contraindicated, and dose separation is not recommended. Similarly, aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases atazanavir solubility. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If atazanavir must be administered, it should be taken 2 hours before or 1 hour after antacids. Aluminum hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide can reduce the absorption of baloxavir marboxil by binding to polyvalent cations in the GI tract. This interaction decreases plasma levels of baloxavir, as shown in animal studies. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and it is recommended to separate ciprofloxacin administration by at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after taking aluminum hydroxide. Similarly, magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of demeclocycline and doxycycline by inhibiting their GI absorption. These interactions also apply only to oral forms, and administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide can increase the levels of digoxin by raising gastric pH, which enhances its absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of eltrombopag by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction is contraindicated, and administration should be separated by at least 4 hours. Similarly, aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of gemifloxacin, ofloxacin, and moxifloxacin by inhibiting their GI absorption. These interactions apply only to oral forms, and administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of nimodipine, nisoldipine, and nitrendipine by raising gastric pH, which enhances their absorption. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of pazopanib and ponatinib by increasing gastric pH, which reduces their solubility. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If co-administration cannot be avoided, pazopanib or ponatinib should be taken 2 hours before and after antacids. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of acalabrutinib by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Similarly, aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of acebutolol, atenolol, and bisoprolol by inhibiting their GI absorption. These interactions apply only to oral forms, and administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of amphetamine and dextroamphetamine by altering renal tubular reabsorption in basic urine. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of dolutegravir by binding to cations in the GI tract. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after taking magnesium hydroxide. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of itraconazole and ketoconazole by inhibiting their GI absorption. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of gabapentin and gabapentin enacarbil by inhibiting their GI absorption. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of glipizide and glyburide by raising gastric pH, which enhances their absorption. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of iron supplements (e.g., ferrous fumarate, ferrous sulfate) by increasing gastric pH, which decreases their solubility. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of isoniazid by inhibiting its GI absorption. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of erythromycin derivatives (e.g., erythromycin base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate) by an unknown mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of crizotinib by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of cyclosporine by inhibiting its GI absorption. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of delafloxacin by binding to cations in the GI tract. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after taking magnesium hydroxide. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of flecainide by altering renal tubular reabsorption in basic urine. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases its solubility. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of gabapentin by inhibiting its GI absorption. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of gefitinib by increasing gastric pH, which decreases its solubility. Administration should be separated by at least 6 hours. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of gemifloxacin by inhibiting its GI absorption. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of glipizide and glyburide by raising gastric pH, which enhances their absorption. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of ibandronate by inhibiting its GI absorption. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of isoniazid by inhibiting its GI absorption. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of itraconazole by inhibiting its GI absorption. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of ketoconazole by inhibiting its GI absorption. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of labetalol by inhibiting its GI absorption. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of lactulose by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases ledipasvir solubility. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours.
